attribution.note: Marcus writes and endorses this summary of the study's findings in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both statistics, the ~30-step condition, the memory-augmented subgroup and the attribution to the study.

contract.note: Scoring on what the study reported, using reputable reports when the paper is unavailable, is a fair plain reading. The separate 67%-at-15-steps figure points to a second drift measure, not a conflict.

evidence.note: ISMG report dated 8 May 2026 quotes the lead author. It gives 94% poisoning among memory-retaining agents and nearly 90% drift after roughly 30 steps, which is consistent with 89.4%.
Wallstreetcn, 6 May 2026, gives exactly 89.4% after about 30 steps and 94% for memory-augmented agents. It cites Marcus, so it may be partly derivative, but it also adds detail beyond his post.

reviews.rationale: Two reports of the study agree with both figures. ISMG, which quotes the lead author directly, independently confirms nearly 90% drift after ~30 steps and 94% poisoning vulnerability. Wallstreetcn gives the exact 89.4%. The primary paper is not in the packet, but the contract accepts reputable reports. No evidence contradicts the claim.

contract.note: Counting a February 2026 revision as 'showed in February' is slightly generous, since v1 dates from Sept 2025. Even so, the paper's v2 was posted in February, and the substance (similar vulnerabilities) does not depend on the date.

evidence.note: STAC v2 on arXiv, revised 2 Feb 2026, reports over 90% attack success for tool-chaining against agents including GPT-4.1.
The STAC v3 author list (July 2026, before the evaluation date) confirms the UC Berkeley and AWS AI Labs affiliations.
ISMG reports that the AWS/UC Berkeley February paper documented the same dynamic, and that the new study added production scale.

reviews.rationale: The AWS/Berkeley STAC paper, with a version dated February 2026, documents over 90% agent vulnerability to tool-chaining attacks, the same class as the new study's 91% finding. ISMG independently draws the same link. The only nuance is that the paper first appeared in Sept 2025.
